SpellcastingCharisma is the casting stat. You never prepare spells: you cast from a fixed Spells Known list, using whichever open slot fits, decided turn by turn. You have one slot fewer than the Wizard wherever the Wizard has three or more (see the Spell Progression table below). Spells Known are fixed until retrained (and see Shifting Blood).
CastingSpend a slot of the appropriate level to cast any spell from your Spells Known list; no daily preparation. As with every caster, a higher-level slot can substitute for a lower-level spell with no extra power (potency always scales by caster level, never by slot spent).
Bloodline KitAt character creation choose a Bloodline Kit. This defines your magical origin and grants a 1st-level Bloodline Ability and a 10th-level Bloodline Awakening.
IdentityMagic in the blood, bent at will: every spell can be twinned, quickened or pushed further, at a price paid in flesh or risk.

Class Abilities

1st Level

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast spontaneously from your Spells Known list using any open slot of the right level. No preparation: casting works exactly like any other caster's slots.

Bloodline Ability

  • Effect: A benefit from your chosen Bloodline Kit. See the Bloodline Kits section.

Metamagic

  • Effect: You know three Metamagic options from the list below, and learn one more at 5th, 10th and 15th level.
  • When you cast a spell you may apply one option you know: burn 2 points with Spellburn for its base effect, or use a Wild Surge for its enhanced effect.
  • One option per spell (from 20th level, once a day, two, paying for each).
  • Spellburn: lower your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution by 2, your choice each time.
  • You burn your own score: a spell, potion, item or form that raises or sets the score gives you nothing more to burn, and burned points stay burned beneath it.
  • A burned score uses its lowered value for everything, Max HP and the death threshold included; if your HP is above your new maximum, it drops to it.
  • Spellburn can't take a score below 1 and never calls for a Corruption roll.
  • Recovery: after a long rest you regain 3 burned points in all, split as you choose (6 from 6th level). Nothing else restores them.
  • Wild Surge: once a day (twice from 5th level, four times from 15th), give a spell an option's enhanced effect at no cost in points.
  • The GM then rolls d20 in secret: on a 1, a Major Corruption; on 2 to 5, a Minor Corruption; on 6 or more, nothing, and the GM tells you the surge passed cleanly.
  • For a Corruption the GM rolls d100 on the Sorcerer's Corruption tables (Monsters & Treasure), which stay GM-only: you know something has shifted, not what.
  • What Corruption can do: a Minor Corruption is a small change that can be cosmetic, helpful or harmful, and may fade.
  • A Major Corruption is lasting.
  • For example: eyes that glow in the dark, frost on everything you touch, a voice that echoes, or a limb that withers.

Metamagic Options

  • Twinned Spell: a spell that targets only one creature and allows a save or needs a touch attack can target a second creature in range with the same casting; each is affected as normal. Enhanced: a third creature as well.
  • Careful Spell: up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) creatures you choose automatically succeed on their save against the spell. Enhanced: they take no effect at all.
  • Empowered Spell: reroll up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) damage dice and keep the new results. Enhanced: reroll any number of the damage dice and keep the new results.
  • Extended Spell: double the duration. Enhanced: triple it, to a maximum of 24 hours.
  • Heightened Spell: one target has Disadvantage on its first save against the spell. Enhanced: all targets do. Against a kill effect, once per encounter.
  • Distant Spell: double the range; touch spells extend to 30ft, and an unwilling target still needs the touch attack. Enhanced: triple the range; touch extends to 60ft.
  • Subtle Spell: cast with no words or gestures; no one can tell you cast it. Enhanced: it also cannot be counterspelled.
  • Flexible Spell: freely change the damage type of the spell to any other type. Enhanced: it also ignores resistance to the new type.
  • Quickened Spell: cast the spell and one cantrip with the same action; no other spell can be cast that turn (the Fey-touched Awakening's extra spell aside). It has no enhanced effect: a Wild Surge gives its base effect.

4th Level

Shifting Blood

  • Effect: After a long rest, you may swap one spell you know for another of the same level from the Sorcerer list, or one Metamagic option you know for another.

6th Level

Blood Burn

  • Effect: You regain 6 burned points after a long rest, in place of 3.

8th Level

Overchannel

  • Effect: When you have no slot left of a spell's level, you may still cast it by burning points from your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution equal to the spell's level, split between them as you like.
  • The magic tears through you: after the spell is cast you take 1d6 damage per spell level.
  • Temporary HP absorbs it first, but Resistance and other reductions don't apply.
  • You may add a Metamagic option, paid for as usual.
  • 15th level: once per day, you Overchannel without taking its damage; you still burn the points.

10th Level

Bloodline Awakening

  • Effect: Your bloodline's power deepens. Gain the 10th-level ability from your Bloodline Kit.

Renown: Name

  • Effect: Your deeds are known.
  • Title: Your blood's name (the Stormborn, say).
  • Sages and colleges pay to study your blood: once per Downtime Phase, earn as a skilled trade by sitting for them, or trade a sitting for one question answered from their books.
  • Your first follower, an attendant, joins you.

13th Level

Font of Power

  • Effect: Once a day, spend 10 minutes with a magic item that holds charges and burn 2 points as Spellburn: it regains one charge. An item regains no more than one charge this way between your Downtime Phases, and never more than it was made with.

15th Level

  • Charisma Bonus: permanent +1 Charisma. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Renown: Holding: you may found your family's house as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).
  • Wild Surge (four a day), Overchannel and Metamagic (a sixth option) improve, as their entries say.

17th Level

Blood Draught

  • Effect: Once per Downtime Phase, or once a week on the road, during a long rest, bleed a spell you know of 3rd level or lower into a vial; its slot doesn't return after that rest.
  • You can have one Draught at a time: an old one spoils when you bleed a new one.
  • The drinker is the spell's only target and gains its effect at your level, as if you had cast it on them.
  • A spell that harms its target or covers an area can't be bled.

20th Level

Chaos Incarnate

  • Effect: Once per day, become a conduit of pure chaos: the next three spells you cast this encounter cost no slot, at any level you can cast, and each takes one Metamagic option's enhanced effect at no cost.
  • After the third spell you suffer a Minor Corruption: the GM rolls d20, and on a 1 it is Major instead.

Renown: Bloodline Seat

  • Effect: Your stronghold becomes the house of your blood (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d4 sorcerers of your bloodline (1st level) seek you out. While you hold it, your first Wild Surge each day carries no Corruption roll.
  • Whether or not you hold a Seat, once per day you may apply two Metamagic options to a single spell, paying for each separately (two Wild Surges, two burns, or one of each).

Spells Known

  • Your Spells Known list is every spell you can cast. Each is always ready to cast from any matching slot. Cantrips are always available and never consume a slot.
  • Bonus Spells: Charisma 13–15 grants one extra 1st-level spell known, 16–17 one extra 2nd-level spell known, 18+ one extra 3rd-level spell known, as well as the matching bonus slot (see Spellcasting in Arneyan). Cumulative, and only once your table gives you slots of that level.
  • Retraining: before 4th level, during a Downtime Phase, a Sorcerer may replace one spell they know with another of the same level. From 4th level, see Shifting Blood.

Spells Known: you know a number of cantrips equal to the 0 column, and a number of spells equal to your Sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), of any spell levels you can cast, up to the number of spells on the Sorcerer list.

Bloodline Kits

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Sorcerer folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose one Bloodline Kit at character creation.
  • Your kit defines your magical origin and grants two bloodline cantrips, on top of your 0 column, and two abilities: a 1st-level Bloodline Ability and a Bloodline Awakening at 10th level (the kit's improvement).
  • Your bloodline reshapes what your raw magic does.
  • All DCs a Sorcerer imposes on a target use the standard spell-save formula (see Spellcasting in Arneyan): DC = 10 + half your Sorcerer level (minimum 1) + Charisma modifier.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
